audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-centric specs: P2P networking protocol changes (eth/70), testnet bootstrapping, fork activation and gas repricing (Tangerine Whistle), difficulty bomb delay and block reward changes (Byzantium), and the Ethereum Provider JavaScript API.

misclassified_entities.reason: Parent block is internal blockchain state data, not an external entity. It is produced by the system itself and stored locally.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via eth/70 Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P network peers. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary protocol messages. All data must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Genesis Configuration Server via HTTP
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: HTTP fetch of genesis.json from yolonet.xyz
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External web server providing genesis configuration over HTTP. No authentication or integrity verification mechanism specified. Data could be tampered with in transit.

trusted_external_entities.name: Bootnode via P2P Discovery
trusted_external_entities.rationale: While operated by Ethereum Foundation, the bootnode communicates over unauthenticated P2P protocol. Peer list data must be validated. Bootnode could be impersonated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethstats Server via WebSocket
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Outbound WebSocket connection to ethstats service
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External monitoring service. Outbound data flow (node sends stats), but the server could send malicious responses. No authentication specified.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners submit blocks over unauthenticated P2P network. Block headers, difficulty, and rewards must be fully validated against consensus rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: DoS Attacker via Transactions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Malicious actor crafting transactions with many IO-heavy operations to exhaust node resources. Completely untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Ethereum Provider API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any web page JavaScript can call the injected provider. No authentication on the caller. Provider must enforce authorization for sensitive methods.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Extension via Provider Injection
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Browser extension provider injection into page context
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Browser extension injects provider object. While users choose to install it, the extension could be compromised or malicious. DApps have no way to verify provider authenticity.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Script via Browser Context
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JavaScript access to injected EthereumProvider object
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Third-party scripts in the same browser context can access the provider. Completely untrusted; provider must gate sensitive operations behind user authorization.

trusted_external_entities.name: End User via Wallet UI
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: User approval/rejection of transaction signing requests
trusted_external_entities.rationale: User interacts through wallet UI to approve or reject requests. User decisions are authoritative for their own accounts but user input should still be treated as untrusted data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Developer via Testnet Transaction Submission
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission to testnet (contract deployment, opcode execution)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Developers submit test transactions including experimental opcodes. No authentication; transactions must be validated against EVM rules.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All requested block numbers must be validated against the Paris upgrade boundary (block 15,537,393). Pre-PoS requests must be rejected. Message format and size must be validated to prevent resource exhaustion.

Genesis JSON must be validated for structural integrity and expected parameters. No integrity verification (e.g., checksum) is specified, so the data could be tampered with. Operators should verify genesis hash independently.
Peer list received from bootnode must be treated as untrusted. Peer addresses must be validated. Eclipse attack mitigation (diverse peer selection) is required.
Outbound connection. Responses from the stats server must be validated. Information leakage risk: stats may reveal node identity, sync status, and other operational details.
Full block validation required: difficulty must match EIP-649 computation, block reward must equal 3 ETH post-Byzantium, uncle rewards must be correctly computed. Invalid blocks must be rejected.
Claimed difficulty must be recomputed and verified against expected difficulty using EIP-649 rules (fake block number = max(0, block_number - 3,000,000)). Mismatch must result in block rejection.

Gas costs for IO operations (SLOAD, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, CALL, etc.) must be set per EIP-150 post-Tangerine Whistle to prevent resource exhaustion attacks. Transactions exceeding gas limits must be reverted.

Provider must validate RequestArguments structure. Sensitive methods (account access, signing) must require explicit user authorization (error 4100 if unauthorized). Method must be supported (error 4200 if not).

DApps cannot verify the authenticity of the injected provider. Users must trust their installed wallet extension. Provider object must be tamper-resistant to prevent page scripts from modifying its behavior.

All requests through the provider must be gated by user authorization for sensitive operations. The provider must not expose private keys or signing capabilities without explicit user consent (error 4001 on rejection, 4100 on unauthorized).
User approval/rejection decisions must be faithfully conveyed. The wallet must display accurate transaction details to the user. Phishing-resistant UI required.
Experimental opcode transactions must be validated against testnet EVM rules. Contract bytecode must be parsed and executed within gas limits. Testnet has no value guarantees.
